## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `08401f6aadc452a1bba675a1de69b94d729b1fd7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md + none

Inputs read: card #33569 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report), PR #33668 (body, 2 files, net diff against merge base `7f0e38a2`), the check-runs on the head, and the cited code on `main` `e9884e19` (read, not reviewed). `main` has moved past the merge base only in two eval JSON files of this skill; `SKILL.md` and every cited code file are unchanged there.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept sets, schemas, runtime behaviour: none changed. The diff is 13 lines of one skill file and one new changeset. Right.
- Public surface: the published text of `@objectstack/skills` changes in item 3 of "Valid-but-silently-wrong". Right, and it is the change the card orders.
- Token ceiling: the PR pays in place (6861 of 6861 claimed, ceiling and line count unmoved). The verdict on that is the token-ratchet and line-ratchet check-runs, not the PR body.
- Check-runs on the head at review time: 41 runs, 14 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 11 still in progress (Test Core 1/8 and 2/8, Live E2E UI, Type Check consumer gates, source gates, debt ledger and workspace, Lint repo and tooling gates, Lint CI release and engine gates, Lint ESLint, Lint docs and code guards). Completed green include Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, the three scoped Lint runs, Dogfood Regression Gate. This record judges the design; the adopting seat reads the 11 pending runs to green before it lets the record carry a merge. A red one among them is a gate FAIL this record does not cover.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` matches what the diff publishes: a wording correction of a skill, no schema, no accept set. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` stand on both the PR body and the changeset, and are right: nothing an author could write before is refused now, nothing is narrowed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Deviation, model tier (dev ran below the mandated tier): answered by this at-tier review.
- Deviation, token payment touching four passages outside the sentence: judged in ④ (N2, N3); accepted.
- Deviation, what the author sees is not written into the sentence: accepted. It follows from "binds NONE" plus the next sentence, and the code agrees: a non-clashing name of the unbound package has no holder and the `script` node fails "no function named ... is registered" (`screen-nodes.ts` L661-668); the clashing name resolves as for a package holding none (runs a dependency's function, or the guard refusal).
- Deviations on the PR signature line and the commit trailer: process, the seat's; no contract effect.
- Out-of-scope findings (stale `hook-binder.ts` L214-216 note; `bareNameColdBootWarning` saying "refused at install" for a function, `registry.ts` L2959-2960): confirmed as described on `main`, correctly left unedited, carrier is the seat. Note the second one is the runtime text an operator reads in the very warning the skill now cites, so it now disagrees with the skill; the follow-up card should not be dropped.
- Old changeset `.changeset/32522-...`: see N1.

### ④ Design judgment

`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md`, the new sentence, claim by claim against `main`:

- "Packages of two namespaces each run their own" (unchanged): holds. `claimBareNameFunctions` passes `incomingNamespace`; `namespacedHoldersMeet` returns false only when both are declared and differ.
- "One namespace (or none)": holds. A package declaring no namespace meets every holder (`namespace-prefix.ts` L224).
- "both held at boot warn `Bare-name conflict at boot`": holds. Before the seal `claimBareNameFunctions` only records (the throw sits inside `if (this.bareNameHoldersSealed)`); the seal runs at `kernel:bootstrapped` and `sealBareNameHoldersAtColdBoot` logs `bareNameColdBootWarning` under `BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE = 'warn'`. Both packages stay bound.
- "a later one installs": holds. After the seal the claim throws `BareNameConflictError` inside `bindHooksToEngine`; `bindAppArtifactHandlers` catches per owner group (L414-444, "Never throws"), and both callers that bind a package (AppPlugin start, install-local `bindArtifactHandlers`) see no throw. No install door judges a function.
- "but binds NONE of its functions or hooks": holds. The claim runs ahead of every `registerFunction` and ahead of the hook loop in the same call, so the owner group's non-clashing functions and all its hooks (body hooks included) are left out. Pinned by `registry-bare-name-one-holder-request-family.test.ts` ("registers nothing", `beta_only_fn` undefined). Correctly limited to functions and hooks: the action half still binds.
- "(error `Failed to bind declarative hooks`)": holds, `logger.error` at `app-artifact-handlers.ts` L442, exact string.
- "rename, or another namespace": rename always works; see N4 for the edge of the second remedy.
- F3: done. The pair held at boot and the holder arriving after boot are two clauses with two different outcomes, each true.

Attempts to break it: a second bind route that would let the throw escape (the two other `bindHooks` callers bind under `metadata-service` with no functions, so they never reach the claim); a package of several owner groups (the catch is per group, and "its" reads per package for the one-group case the sentence addresses); the eval prompts (no eval of this skill cites `FLOW_FAILED`, `innerRefusal`, `normalize_phone` or the boot warning; the `outputVariable` evals are served by the example and by item 2). None breaks the sentence.

Findings: no must-fix, no should-fix.

- N1 (nit, changeset prose). The new changeset states the correction of the unreleased `32522-skills-automation-function-name-per-namespace` entry instead of editing it. Acceptable, and the dev was right not to touch a file outside the claimed surface, but it is the weaker choice: both entries land in one release, so the changelog will print "the later bind is refused at install" and, a few lines away, its retraction. An unreleased changeset is still a draft; amending that one clause (to "the later bind fails and the package's functions and hooks stay unbound") is the cleaner result. Recommended as a one-line follow-up by the seat; not a condition of this PASS.
- N2 (nit). "ownerless" replaces "(registered under no package)". In context ("the platform's ownerless function in every flow's reach", in a paragraph about packages) it reads the same, and the code's own word is "owner-less (platform) function". But the file's two other uses (Assignment rules, L342 and L350) mean a record with no owner, a different thing, so the word now carries two senses in one file. No rule is lost because "the platform's" already carries the meaning.
- N3 (nit). The flow door clause lost `400 FLOW_FAILED` and the `error.details.` path, and the skill has no pointer to `objectstack-api`, where L356-365 teach both and name a `script` node's function-name refusal. An agent holding only this skill still learns the name `innerRefusal` and the in-flow `$error.code`, which is what a flow author needs; the wire shape is the API skill's subject. No authoring rule lost. The `outputVariable` gloss and "(below)" cuts lose nothing: the example and item 2 show both.
- N4 (nit). "another namespace" helps only when both packages end up declaring different namespaces; if the earlier holder declares none, it meets every namespace and only the rename works. The sentence's lead "One namespace (or none)" makes this recoverable. Also unstated: the unbound state lasts until the next cold boot, where the pair is "held at boot", both bind and the warning appears. Neither changes what the author should do.
- N5 (nit, changeset prose). The changeset body says "two restatements are shortened"; the diff shortens four passages (the PR body lists all four).

Nits only: the round ends here. Any nit fix outside the prose faces moves the head and this record no longer covers it.
